The linked anchor (worktrees.md § Copy gitignored files into worktrees) supplies the semantics: `.gitignore` syntax, and only files that both match a pattern and are also gitignored are copied. desktop.md adds no carve-out; the only one anywhere is worktrees.md's, that a `WorktreeCreate` hook replaces the file rather than complementing it.

divergence: The whole mechanism is missing — not a wrong key name, not a narrower glob, not a misspelled field. Nothing opens `<projectRoot>/.worktreeinclude`, nothing parses gitignore syntax for it, nothing asks git which paths are ignored, and no file of any kind is copied into a worktree. Because it is a dotfile rather than a settings key it fails SILENTLY when a user writes it (the equivalent expressed under `worktree.*` in settings.json fails loudly instead — worktree-settings.ts:81). The two adjacent things we do ship are not it: (a) `worktree.symlinkDirectories` (worktree-git-plan.ts:112-124) symlinks instead of copying, takes plain repo-relative paths rather than gitignore patterns, has no "and is also gitignored" filter and defaults empty — an entry naming a file does work today, since SessionManager.ts:10190 only checks `existsSync`, so it is a semantically different partial workaround (writes inside the worktree write through to the main checkout); (b) the `WorktreeCreate` command hook we ship (packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:360, path capture at :1247-1255) is precisely what Claude's docs offer INSTEAD of `.worktreeinclude`, not an implementation of it. Two second-order deltas, both verified: our `WorktreeCreate` hook replaces only the PATH (worktree-lease-service.ts:251-284) and `git.create` still runs afterwards, so the doc's "hook is configured ⇒ do not process `.worktreeinclude`" carve-out has no flag to hang off; and on the `EnterWorktree` trigger the hook is not even fired, because `createSessionWorktreePort` builds the lease service with a no-op emit (`createPiWorktreeLeaseService(managed, async () => {})`, SessionManager.ts:10243) and `createPiWorktreeLeaseService` calls `existing.setEmit(emit)` on the cached service (:10093), so that path has no escape hatch at all. Scope note: this is the desktop-page view of ONE gap that three pages state — f096 (worktrees.md) and f147 (claude-directory.md) are the same missing reader, and the edit list below matches theirs deliberately so the specs cannot drift. One fix, three pages. Separately noted and NOT scoped here: desktop.md:323's premise (every parallel session automatically gets its own worktree) is itself unbuilt in this fork — worktree creation is agent-driven only.

change.what: New pure planner, sibling to worktree-git-plan.ts and in the same 'assertable without a repository, a supervisor and a session' shape that file's header states (:12-13). (1) `parseWorktreeInclude(text: string): WorktreeIncludePattern[]` — gitignore syntax: drop blank lines and `#` comments (`\#` escapes a literal `#`), trim unescaped trailing whitespace, record `negated` for a leading `!`, `anchored` for a leading `/`, `directoryOnly` for a trailing `/`. Reuse the caps from worktree-settings.ts:64-65 (MAX_LIST_ENTRIES 128 / MAX_ENTRY_LENGTH 512) and refuse absolute forms and `..` segments exactly as `repoRelativePaths` does (worktree-settings.ts:91-107) — a project-root file must not be able to name a source outside the repository. (2) `worktreeIncludeCandidateCommands(repoRoot): WorktreeGitCommand[]` (the interface at worktree-git-plan.ts:16-23) producing the candidate set from git itself: `['-C', repoRoot, 'ls-files', '-z', '--others', '--ignored', '--exclude-standard', '--directory', '--no-empty-directory']`, operation `'include-list'`, cwd `'repo'`, `allowFailure: true`; `--directory --no-empty-directory` is what stops a repo with `node_modules` emitting 200k paths, and for every wildcard-free pattern also emit a targeted `['-C', repoRoot, 'check-ignore', '-q', '--', <pattern>]` so a file inside a wholly-collapsed ignored directory stays reachable. Using git as the ignore oracle is what satisfies 'also gitignored' without a second ignore implementation. Do NOT reuse packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/gitignore-glob.ts as the matcher without extending it: `matchGitignoreGlob` (:59-72) implements the documented permissions subset only and has no negation and no last-match-wins. (3) `worktreeIncludePlan({ repoRoot, worktreePath, patterns, ignoredEntries })` → `{ source, destination }[]`, applying gitignore's LAST-matching-pattern-wins with negation and joining against the resolved roots so a destination can only land inside the worktree (same containment argument as worktree-git-plan.ts:105-111).

The single fix point — both product triggers and recovery inherit it. Insert the include step AFTER the `worktreeCreateCommands` loop (so a sparse checkout has materialised, :10185) and beside the existing symlink loop (:10189-10197): read `<root>/.worktreeinclude` where `root = await projectRoot()` (:10113,:10165) — the PROJECT root the page names, unprefixed, NOT the worktree and NOT `.nessy-agent/`. Absent file ⇒ no-op. Run the candidate commands through the existing `runGit` (:10117-10133; its `profile: 'read-only'` and `additionalWritableRoots: [authority.root, authority.namespaceRoot]` at runWorktreeGit :10029-10047 already cover this), split `-z` output on NUL from `result.output`, feed it to `worktreeIncludePlan`, then per pair `mkdir(dirname(destination), { recursive: true })` + `copyFile(source, destination)` and `chmod` to the source's mode — these are secrets, a `.env` at 0600 must not land 0644 — skipping when the destination already exists. Extend the fs import at :15 (`{ readFile, writeFile, mkdir, realpath, symlink }`) with `copyFile`, `chmod`, `stat`. Failure tolerance must copy the symlink precedent immediately below (`sessionLog.warn`, never fail creation), including a malformed `.worktreeinclude`. Skip-if-exists is load-bearing rather than politeness: `recoverUnlocked` re-invokes `git.create` for a `creating` lease (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.ts:290-299), so the step must be idempotent.

Small plumbing for the hook carve-out. Have `applyWorktreeCreateHookPath` additionally report whether it adopted a hook-returned path (it already distinguishes that case at :273-274), and widen `create(lease: WorktreeLeaseV1)` to `create(lease: WorktreeLeaseV1, context: { hookReplacedPath: boolean })`; SessionManager's implementation skips the include step when it is true. Pass it as a CALL ARGUMENT, never as a field on `WorktreeLeaseV1` — that type is persisted (`managed.worktreeLeaseState`, schemaVersion 1, persisted at SessionManager.ts:10137-10142) and adding a field there turns an M into a persistence-boundary change for no gain. `recoverUnlocked`'s call at :296 passes `{ hookReplacedPath: false }`.

Two representative cases per the repo's minimum-test budget, table-driven where it collapses: (positive) a `.worktreeinclude` of `.env` plus `!.env.production` against a candidate set containing both, asserting only `.env` is planned and the destination is inside the worktree; (negative/boundary) a pattern naming a TRACKED file, a pattern with `..`, and an absolute pattern — the first produces no plan entry because it is not in the ignored candidate set, the other two are refused at parse. Mirror the existing shape in packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.test.ts.

Mechanical: both files build fake `git: { create, inspect, remove }` ports, so the widened `create` arity has to be accepted there. No behavioural assertion changes; if either test asserts the argument list of `create`, add the `{ hookReplacedPath: false }` second argument.

Both product triggers inherit the fix without their own edit — `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/worktree.ts:19,:53 → SessionManager.ts:10269) and subagent `isolation: worktree` (SessionManager.ts:10334-10347) — so there is one fix point, not three. NO wire or schema boundary is crossed PROVIDED the hook flag rides the call argument; putting it on `WorktreeLeaseV1` would cross the persisted `worktreeLeaseState` boundary (schemaVersion 1) and is rejected in the edit list. There IS a security boundary, and it is what review must gate: this becomes the first path that copies gitignored SECRETS out of the main checkout into `<dirname(repoRoot)>/.nessy-worktrees/<repo-slug>/<leaseId>/`, a directory that outlives the session until the orphan sweep removes it (packages/shared/src/sessions/worktree-orphans.ts, driven from SessionManager.ts:10759 `sweepOrphanedWorktrees`), and a subagent under `isolation: worktree` is precisely the actor previously denied those files. Mode preservation (`chmod` to the source's mode) and destination containment are the two review gates. The git reads go through `runWorktreeGit`'s supervised `profile: 'read-only'` child (SessionManager.ts:10029-10047), so no new process-spawn surface is introduced.
userImpact: Two different experiences, and only one is observable today. On the desktop surface this sentence actually sits in, it is latent because the premise is missing too: a user who clicks + New session gets no worktree at all in this fork, so `.worktreeinclude` has nothing to affect — writing the file produces no error and no effect. What IS observable today is the agent-driven path. A project keeping local config in a gitignored `.env` runs a subagent with `isolation: worktree`, or the model calls `EnterWorktree`, and the worktree comes up without it: `bun run dev`, a test run, a migration or any script reading `.env` fails inside the worktree with missing-variable errors while the identical command works in the main checkout, and nothing in the transcript says a file was not carried over. The documented remedy fails silently — the dotfile has no reader — while expressing the same intent as a settings key fails loudly with `invalid worktree setting` (packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:81). The workarounds that do work are undiscoverable and semantically different: listing the path under `worktree.symlinkDirectories` yields a symlink whose edits write back into the main checkout, or the user hand-writes a `WorktreeCreate` command hook — and that second one does not cover `EnterWorktree` at all, since that path installs a no-op emit (SessionManager.ts:10243). Building automatic per-session desktop worktrees would immediately surface the latent half.
